episode.title: Align grapheme-cluster width estimates with terminal cell allocation
episode.before: At parent 2c3041242040179b63841922ac58188f8499d2cd, terminal width calculation assigned each grapheme the width of its first visible code point, with extra accounting only for trailing halfwidth/fullwidth forms and Thai/Lao AM vowels. Indic consonants following marks and most terminal-spacing marks inside a grapheme were therefore omitted, causing measured line widths to be smaller than the cells allocated by wcwidth-style terminals.
episode.after: At dfe47d3fbd8bf27841becaf8ec042dc0e73804a6, width calculation recognizes Unicode spacing marks plus selected legacy wcwidth exceptions, counts those marks as terminal cells, and counts visible continuation characters occurring after marks. Ordinary combining marks, specified zero-width exceptions, CJK/Japanese widths, Thai/Lao behavior, and selected Myanmar zero-width combinations remain covered by regression assertions.
episode.diff: The change added per-code-point classifiers for non-printing characters, marks, and terminal-spacing marks; handled terminal-spacing mark-only clusters before the general zero-width rule; replaced the narrow trailing-character loop with a stateful scan that counts spacing marks and visible characters following marks; and added 43 lines of width regression tests spanning Indic scripts, ordinary combining marks, CJK/Japanese text, Thai/Lao vowels, and Myanmar marks.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned commit dfe47d3f resolves PR #6987 with an implementation and tests, and identifies parent 2c3041242040179b63841922ac58188f8499d2cd.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json; git show --format=fuller dfe47d3fbd8bf27841becaf8ec042dc0e73804a6; git rev-parse dfe47d3fbd8bf27841becaf8ec042dc0e73804a6^

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation derived a grapheme's width from its first visible code point and only added widths for trailing U+FF00–U+FFEF forms or Thai/Lao AM vowels; all-mark clusters passed through the zero-width rule.
evidence_units.source: git show 2c3041242040179b63841922ac58188f8499d2cd:packages/tui/src/utils.ts, graphemeWidth and its character-classification regexes

evidence_units.claim: The implementation introduced classifiers for individual non-printing characters and marks, plus a terminal-spacing-mark set based on Unicode Spacing_Mark with U+1734/U+302E/U+302F exclusions and selected legacy wcwidth exceptions.

The new grapheme scan adds one cell for each classified terminal-spacing mark and adds the East Asian width of a visible continuation after a mark, while continuing to ignore other non-printing characters.

The corrected width primitive feeds terminal overflow checks, viewport clipping, selection column mapping, slicing, wrapping, truncation, and component padding, so its cell estimate controls multiple rendering boundaries.
evidence_units.source: git grep at dfe47d3fbd8bf27841becaf8ec042dc0e73804a6 for visibleWidth/graphemeWidth; packages/tui/src/TuiMainScreen.ts:413-435; packages/tui/src/TuiAltScreen.ts:300-358; packages/tui/src/components/box.ts:128

evidence_units.claim: Regression assertions require widths of two cells for conjunct examples across Devanagari, Bengali, Gujarati, Odia, Telugu, and Malayalam, and verify representative Devanagari words and a sentence.
evidence_units.source: git show dfe47d3fbd8bf27841becaf8ec042dc0e73804a6:packages/tui/test/truncate-to-width.test.ts, test 'counts Indic conjunct spacing code points within grapheme clusters'

evidence_units.claim: Regression assertions preserve zero-width behavior for ordinary combining marks and specified exceptions, and preserve existing CJK and Japanese width results.
evidence_units.source: git show dfe47d3fbd8bf27841becaf8ec042dc0e73804a6:packages/tui/test/truncate-to-width.test.ts, tests 'keeps ordinary combining marks zero-width' and 'keeps CJK and Japanese width accounting unchanged'

evidence_units.claim: Regression assertions distinguish Myanmar marks allocated terminal cells from combinations expected to remain one cell wide.
evidence_units.source: git show dfe47d3fbd8bf27841becaf8ec042dc0e73804a6:packages/tui/test/truncate-to-width.test.ts, test 'counts Myanmar marks that terminals allocate cells for'

evidence_units.claim: The changed test file provides direct numeric visibleWidth assertions for affected scripts and unaffected width classes; the evidence bundle classifies the resolution as implementation_plus_test, but no pinned-ref CI or local passing result is available in the bundle.
evidence_units.source: packages/tui/test/truncate-to-width.test.ts at dfe47d3fbd8bf27841becaf8ec042dc0e73804a6; issue-bundle.json manifest_metadata.quality and provenance.verification

evidence_units.claim: The commit documents the calculation as a compatibility heuristic that favors overcounting to avoid terminal autowrap; Kitty may overcount some clusters, terminal mode 2027 does not report cluster widths, and OSC 66 support was not implemented.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile_grapheme_width_with_terminal_cells
candidate_atomics.title: Reconcile grapheme width with terminal cell allocation
candidate_atomics.description: Refine a grapheme-based width estimator by identifying code points that terminals advance separately and counting visible continuations after marks without converting ordinary combining marks into cells.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent terminal layout from underestimating the cells occupied by multi-code-point grapheme clusters.
semantic_action.module_role: terminal cell-width estimator shared by layout and rendering operations
semantic_action.pre_state: A grapheme cluster is measured primarily from its first visible code point, so terminal-spacing marks and visible consonants following marks can occupy uncounted cells.
semantic_action.post_state: Each recognized terminal-spacing mark and each qualifying visible continuation contributes to the cluster's width, while unrelated non-printing marks retain zero additional width.
semantic_action.validation: Evaluate numeric width assertions for affected Indic and Myanmar clusters and confirm the shared consumers receive the corrected estimate.

candidate_atomics.name: validate_unicode_width_boundaries
candidate_atomics.title: Validate corrected and preserved Unicode width boundaries
candidate_atomics.description: Use script-specific numeric assertions to prove the targeted width increase while guarding combining-mark, CJK, Japanese, Thai/Lao, and Myanmar exceptions against collateral changes.

semantic_action.intent: Demonstrate that the terminal-width correction covers the failing cluster shapes without broadly changing established Unicode width behavior.
semantic_action.pre_state: The revised classifier and scan could accidentally assign cells to ordinary combining marks or alter unrelated wide-character behavior.
semantic_action.post_state: Affected clusters have explicit expected cell counts and unaffected or exceptional clusters retain their prior expected counts.
semantic_action.validation: Run the focused truncate-to-width test file and require every visibleWidth equality assertion to pass.

candidate_workflows.name: correct_terminal_width_for_multi_codepoint_graphemes
candidate_workflows.title: Correct terminal widths for multi-code-point graphemes
candidate_workflows.description: Adjust a shared terminal width estimator when Unicode grapheme segmentation groups code points that the target terminal model advances across multiple cells, then validate both corrected cases and preserved boundaries.

workflow_graph.goal: Make layout width estimates match the conservative cell allocation of wcwidth-style terminals closely enough to prevent horizontal drift and accidental autowrap.
when_to_use: A terminal UI measures text by grapheme clusters but observed rendering advances farther than the computed width.
Failures involve marks, conjuncts, or visible continuations grouped into one grapheme by Unicode segmentation.
The same width primitive controls clipping, padding, wrapping, selection, or overflow checks.
anti_goals: Do not equate every Unicode mark with a terminal cell.
Do not change established emoji, CJK, Japanese, ANSI-sequence, or ordinary combining-mark behavior without evidence.
Do not cap repeated spacing or continuation contributions when the terminal model may advance for each one.
Do not treat this heuristic as exact for every terminal implementation.
not_applicable_when: The renderer obtains authoritative cell widths from the terminal or an applicable protocol.
The mismatch is caused by ANSI parsing, tab expansion, font shaping, bidi layout, or normalization rather than grapheme-to-cell accounting.
No reproducible expected cell counts or terminal behavior can establish a validation oracle.
inputs: Representative failing grapheme clusters and expected cell counts
The terminal compatibility policy, including whether undercounting or overcounting is more damaging
workflow_graph.entry_state: Unicode segmentation is correct at the grapheme boundary, but the width estimator undercounts code points that some supported terminals allocate separate cells.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The shared estimator counts evidence-backed terminal-spacing code points and post-mark visible continuations, and focused regressions confirm affected and preserved width classes.

steps.condition: Use when one grapheme can contain multiple code points that the supported terminal model advances separately.
steps.validation: Inspect the estimator to confirm spacing marks are handled before the general zero-width rule and the trailing scan only adds evidence-backed spacing or visible continuation widths.

steps.condition: Always required after changing the shared cell-width estimator.
steps.validation: The focused numeric assertions must cover affected Indic and Myanmar examples plus ordinary combining-mark and CJK/Japanese controls.

validation_ladder: Check direct numeric widths for minimal affected grapheme clusters.
Check words or sentences containing repeated affected clusters to expose accumulated drift.
Check ordinary combining marks and explicit zero-width exceptions.
Check unrelated wide-character classes such as CJK and Japanese text.
Check the focused width test file in the pinned implementation environment; a passing execution result remains unavailable in the supplied evidence.
stop_conditions: Stop if the before-state undercount cannot be reproduced or inferred directly from the parent implementation.
Stop if expected cell counts cannot be grounded in tests or observed supported-terminal behavior.
Defer a universal correction when supported terminals disagree and no compatibility policy selects the acceptable bias.
Do not promote this single-episode workflow into a cross-project resolution pattern without independent workflows and holdout validation.
unresolved_or_deferred: The heuristic can overcount some Indic continuations in Kitty while matching xterm-style advancement.
OSC 66, which could provide a preferable supported-terminal mechanism, was explicitly not implemented.
Mode 2027 does not provide cluster widths, so local estimation remains necessary.
A passing test execution or CI status for the pinned ref is not present in the supplied evidence.

unresolved_questions: GitHub issue/PR body, comments, reviews, timeline, and status checks were unavailable in the evidence bundle.
The linked commit says it fixes issue #6124 while the extraction identity is PR #6987; the bundle establishes the PR/commit link but not the original issue discussion.
No authoritative cross-terminal specification establishes one exact width for every covered cluster; the implementation deliberately chooses a conservative compatibility heuristic.
No successful focused-test execution at the pinned ref was established from the available checkout and bundle, so validation is grounded in committed assertions rather than a recorded passing run.
